parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, facility ban, border restriction or current organised targeting; same-sex conduct is legal and 2024 equal-treatment law is a climate signal. If outed, main exposures are social hostility and custody: a 2024 mob of ~150 attacked two trans people (21 arrests, outcome unsourced) and religious opposition plus transphobic public comments show threat-framing, not just friction. The 2013 police stops/mistreatment of trans sex workers with discontinued complaints is dated state impunity. Custody defaults to registered sex with isolation, but an individual transfer route to a women's facility was documented and used in 2021. A 2017 attack led to convictions on appeal, showing some recourse works. Protective machinery is largely on paper without documented visitor-service enforcement, and the LGBT-wide fear survey is not trans-specific prevalence. This places it in reduced-risk, below acceptance-with-working-remedies tiers.
